title: Athenian Democracy (508-322 BCE)
description: Athenian democracy, founded by Cleisthenes' reforms (508 BCE), gave male citizens direct votes in the Assembly, with the Council of 500 chosen by lot and large juries deciding trials. It excluded women, enslaved people, and non-citizens — a fraction of the population ruled. Macedonian conquest ended it in 322 BCE, but its ideals of citizen participation shaped every democracy since.
demo:
print('Athens 508-322 BCE: Assembly votes, Council of 500 by lot, big juries')
print('citizens only (fraction of population); ended by Macedon 322 BCE')

title: Roman Republic to Empire
description: The Roman Republic (509-27 BCE) balanced consuls, Senate, and popular assemblies until civil wars collapsed it; Augustus founded the Empire (27 BCE), keeping republican forms while concentrating power. The imperial system — emperor, bureaucracy, standing army — ruled the Mediterranean for centuries. Rome's arc from republic to empire remains the classic study of how republics fail.

print('Republic 509-27 BCE (consuls/Senate/assemblies) -> Empire 27 BCE (Augustus)')
print('the classic study of how republics fail')

title: Chinese Dynastic System to PRC
description: China's imperial system ran from Qin unification (221 BCE) through the Qing dynasty's fall (1912), governed by the emperor with a Confucian scholar-bureaucracy chosen by examination — history's first meritocratic civil service. The 1911 revolution founded the Republic; the Communist victory in 1949 founded the People's Republic, a one-party socialist state that kept the centralized bureaucratic tradition in new form.
demo:
print('Qin 221 BCE -> Qing 1912: emperor + examination bureaucracy')
print('1911 republic; 1949 PRC: one-party state, centralized tradition continues')

title: Pharaonic Egypt to Modern Egypt
description: Pharaonic Egypt united under Narmer (c. 3100 BCE) into a divine-kingship state lasting three millennia through Old, Middle, and New Kingdoms. Persian, Greek (Ptolemaic), Roman, Arab, Ottoman, and British rule followed; independence came in 1922 (fuller in 1953 as a republic). Modern Egypt is a presidential republic whose ancient bureaucracy's centralized habits echo across 5,000 years.

print('Narmer c.3100 BCE -> 3000 yrs of pharaohs -> Persians/Greeks/Romans/Arabs/Ottomans/British')
print('republic 1953; centralized habits echo 5000 years')

title: Persian Empires to Islamic Republic
description: Persia's Achaemenid Empire (550-330 BCE) built history's first great bureaucracy with satrapies and royal roads; the Sassanids (224-651 CE) followed before the Arab conquest brought Islam. The Safavids (1501-1736) made Shi'a Islam the state creed; the Pahlavi shahs (1925-1979) modernized by decree until the 1979 revolution founded the Islamic Republic — a theocratic republic combining elected institutions with clerical oversight.

print('1979: Islamic Republic — elected institutions + clerical oversight')

title: Holy Roman Empire (800/962-1806)
description: The Holy Roman Empire — Charlemagne crowned 800, Otto I's refounding 962 — was a decentralized patchwork of German princes, bishops, and free cities under an elected emperor, famously 'neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire' (Voltaire). The Reformation and Thirty Years' War (1618-48) shattered its unity; Napoleon dissolved it in 1806. Its thousand-year run shaped German federal instincts.

print('dissolved by Napoleon 1806; shaped German federalism')

title: Venetian Republic (697-1797)
description: The Republic of Venice endured a thousand years (traditionally 697-1797) as a merchant oligarchy: a Doge elected for life, councils of nobles, and elaborate checks against any one family seizing power. It grew rich on East-West trade and built a maritime empire. Napoleon ended it in 1797; its longevity remains the record for a republican system.

title: Aztec Triple Alliance (1428-1521)
description: The Aztec Empire was a Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan from 1428, ruling central Mexico through tribute, with the Mexica huey tlatoani (emperor) dominant. Its chinampa agriculture fed a capital larger than contemporary London. Cortés's 1519-1521 conquest, with Indigenous allies and smallpox, ended it; its tribute bureaucracy was absorbed by Spanish colonial rule.

print('Triple Alliance 1428-1521: tribute empire; Tenochtitlan > London in size')

title: Inca Empire (c. 1438-1533)
description: The Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu) grew from c. 1438 under Pachacuti into the Andes' great state, run by the Sapa Inca with decimal administration, 40,000 km of roads, and storehouse redistribution — without writing or markets as Europe knew them. Civil war weakened it before Pizarro's 1532-33 conquest. Its roads and terraces still shape the Andes.

title: Ottoman Government to Turkish Republic
description: The Ottoman Empire was ruled by the sultan with the Grand Vizier, the divan council, and the millet system administering religious communities. The 19th-century Tanzimat reforms tried constitutional modernization; the 1908 Young Turk revolution restored parliament. Defeat in WWI ended the sultanate (1922); Atatürk's 1923 republic replaced it with a secular presidential-parliamentary system.

title: British Parliamentary Evolution
description: Britain's government evolved from Magna Carta (1215) and the 1689 Bill of Rights through the Great Reform Act (1832) and universal suffrage (1928) into a constitutional monarchy with parliamentary sovereignty. The prime minister commands the Commons majority; the monarch reigns but does not rule. The Westminster model was exported across the Commonwealth.

title: French Republics (1792-Present)
description: France has cycled through five republics since 1792: the First (revolution), Second (1848), Third (1870-1940, the long parliamentary one), Fourth (1946-58), and Fifth (1958-present, de Gaulle's semi-presidential system with a strong president). Monarchies and empires interrupted the sequence twice. The Fifth Republic's hybrid executive remains the current frame.

title: Meiji Japan (1868-1947)
description: Meiji Japan transformed a feudal shogunate into a modern state in decades: the 1868 Restoration returned power to the emperor, the 1889 constitution created an elected Diet alongside imperial sovereignty, and industrialization made Japan a great power by 1905. The system ended with the 1947 postwar constitution, which made the emperor a symbol and sovereignty reside with the people.

title: Soviet Government (1917-1991)
description: Soviet government ran through the Communist Party's monopoly: soviets (councils) as the formal base, the Party Congress and Central Committee above, and the Politburo/General Secretary holding real power. The 1936 and 1977 constitutions promised rights the one-party system did not deliver. Gorbachev's reforms (1985-91) unintentionally dissolved the system it meant to save.

title: United States Federal Government (1789-Present)
description: The U.S. federal government under the 1789 Constitution divides power among the presidency, Congress (House + Senate), and the federal judiciary, with federalism splitting authority between Washington and the states. Amendments ended slavery (13th), guaranteed equal protection (14th), and extended suffrage to all adult citizens. It is the world's oldest continuous constitutional republic.
